title: Invertibility of the explicit expression coefficient transpose
statement: Fix prime l, finite E/Q_l, D, o, and primitives d [def-sf-integral-expression-recursion-data]. Suppose rec: Reconstruction supplies reduction and limit closure and invertibility of the actual unit and counit on the specified constructible and Good domains. For every typed finite expression e with its geometric conditions and K in e.domain [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain], the component transposeComparison(d,e)_K is an isomorphism. The associated canonicalComparisons is defined as the inverse of this explicit natural transformation; the inverse adjunction hom-set equivalence gives its whole-system coefficient identity. This statement asserts neither the unary/tensor recursion equations nor direct compactification agreement.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence; agent-formulated expression-tree refinement, lem-sf-integral-expression-recursion, proof steps 1--11.

proof.text: At a variable, transposeComparison is the actual unit because coefficientMap is identity. Reconstruction.unit applies to the constructible input. The coefficientTransformation_app theorem identifies the natural and component recursions.

Inductively write H for the child integral value and M for its system value. Its transpose H -> L M is an isomorphism. Since M is Good, Reconstruction.limit implies L M is constructible. Reconstruction.reduction and the invertible counit at M give Good R L M; Good A M transports across A(e_M) to Good A R L M. Thus d_A at L M has exactly its basicUnaryDomain witness. Counit naturality and unaryTranspose identify the parent transpose with A_int of the child transpose followed by d_A(L M)^(-1) and L A(e_M). Every factor is invertible. Good and constructibility transport along isomorphisms by transporting normalization, cohomological and Tor intervals, and the compatible Origins evaluation isomorphisms; the quotient squares remain true by naturality.

For tensor perform the same calculation with the pair of child isomorphisms and B(e_M,e_N), using tensorTranspose. Both tensor branches are strictly smaller even when variables repeat. For compact support do the open unary step followed by the proper unary step. The intermediate open Good condition belongs to e.domain; properness over the finite-type root gives the finite-type compactification scheme.

theorem transposeComparison_isIso (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (o : Operations l E) (d : Primitives l E D o) (rec : Reconstruction l E D)
    {I : Type u} {X : I → Over (Spec (.of D.k))}
    {W : Over (Spec (.of D.k))} (e : Expression _ I X W) (g : e.geometric)
    (K : (e.domain l E o).FullSubcategory) :
    IsIso ((transposeComparison l E d e g).app K)
